questions.question: What specificity problem does strict BEM (one class per selector, no nesting) solve?
options: It keeps every selector at the same specificity level (0,1,0), so source order determines the cascade predictably instead of selectors fighting to 'out-specify' each other
It removes the need for a build tool
It automatically generates unique class names
questions.explanation: Specificity wars happen when selectors of different specificity override each other unpredictably; BEM avoids this by convention, keeping every rule equally specific.

questions.question: How does utility-first CSS (Tailwind) avoid the 'what do I name this class?' problem that BEM still has?
options: It doesn't — naming is still required
Styles are composed directly in markup from small, pre-existing utility classes, so there's no custom class to invent or name at all
It auto-generates BEM-style names for you
It only works with inline styles, not classes
questions.explanation: Utility classes are reused and composed rather than authored per component, removing the naming-invention step entirely — at the cost of more verbose markup.

questions.question: How does a CSS Module guarantee that `.title` in one component's stylesheet never collides with `.title` in another's?
options: By convention — developers must remember not to reuse names
The build tool rewrites each class name into a unique generated identifier scoped to that file, enforced automatically rather than by discipline
CSS Modules don't actually prevent collisions
By wrapping styles in a unique ID on every page
questions.explanation: Unlike BEM, which relies on a team following a naming convention, CSS Modules enforce scoping mechanically at build time, so a naming mistake can't cause an actual collision.

questions.question: What is the main trade-off utility-first CSS makes compared to BEM or CSS Modules?
options: It cannot be purged of unused styles
More verbose markup and a vocabulary of utility class names to learn, in exchange for eliminating naming/file-organization decisions
It requires a runtime JavaScript library to work
It cannot be combined with any other CSS approach
questions.explanation: Utility-first CSS trades visually noisier HTML/JSX for removing an entire category of decisions (naming, file structure) that the other two approaches still require.
